hints: Look at the moles of gas on each side and the sign of ΔH, as both tell you which way equilibrium will shift.
Count 3 moles of gas on the left but only 2 moles on the right, so higher pressure must favour the side with fewer moles.
Remember that a catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, so ask yourself if it can change yield or Kp.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 with pressure**

Count the gas moles. Left has 3 moles ($2\text{SO}_2 + 1\text{O}_2$) and right has 2 moles ($2\text{SO}_3$).

Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles to reduce pressure, so it shifts right and yield of $\text{SO}_3$ increases. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 with temperature**

The forward reaction is exothermic because $\Delta H = -197 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

$$2\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(\text{g})$$

Increasing temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction, so the position shifts left and $K_p$ gets smaller. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 with catalyst**

A vanadium(V) oxide catalyst lowers activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions by the same amount.

It makes equilibrium reached faster but does not change the position, the yield, or the value of $K_p$. Statement 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

That combination matches option B.

options.A: This option claims all three statements are correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but statement 3 is wrong because a catalyst never changes equilibrium yield, it only increases rate.
options.B: This option states that only 1 and 2 are correct. Higher pressure favours 2 moles of SO3 over 3 moles of reactants, and higher temperature shifts the exothermic equilibrium left so Kp falls. Catalyst has no effect on yield.
options.C: This option includes statement 3 and omits statement 1. Statement 3 is false as catalyst does not increase yield, and statement 1 is true and should not be omitted.
options.D: This option includes only statement 1. While statement 1 is true, statement 2 is also true because increasing temperature for an exothermic reaction decreases Kp, so this option is incomplete.
